findings.source_en: Though the author’s name is lost, his words live on. He who held the seeds of infinity in his palm, made a promise. If he could not end what he started, he would find another way. The scripture pledges to cleanse the Revered, but such claims remain untested.
findings.ar: ضاع اسم كاتبه، لكن كلماته بقيت حيّة. هو الذي حمل بذور الخلود في راحته وقطع عهدًا: إن لم يستطع إنهاء ما بدأه، فسيجد طريقًا آخر. يتعهّد هذا النص بتطهير المُكرَّمين، غير أن هذه الدعاوى لم تُختبر بعد.
findings.issue: 'seeds of infinity' became بذور الخلود (seeds of immortality). Infinity is اللانهاية throughout this corpus - 'Children of Infinity' is أبناء اللانهاية, including on key /GenessaCenserFlavorText in this same chunk. The rendering severs the link between this author and the Children of Infinity, which is the whole point of the item.
findings.suggested_ar: ضاع اسم كاتبه، لكن كلماته بقيت حيّة. هو الذي حمل بذور اللانهاية في راحته وقطع عهدًا: إن لم يستطع إنهاء ما بدأه، فسيجد طريقًا آخر. يتعهّد هذا النص بتطهير المُكرَّمين، غير أن هذه الدعاوى لم تُختبر بعد.

findings.issue: The antecedent is 'the notes'. The namespace is HasNotes_10 and it contains only two rows - this one and 'The notes… for the serum?' - so the unnamed 'it' is the notes. الملاحظات is a feminine plural in Arabic, so the pronoun should be ـها, not ـه. As written the question points at some unnamed masculine object. (Co-location in the namespace, not row order - these keys are hash-tailed and carry no sequence.)
'I've been tracking him' is ongoing up to now; كنتُ أتعقّبه closes the action off in the past. The surrounding lines ('We find him… Sariel.' / 'We kill him.') show Ruk is still on the hunt.
